Delete one verifier CALL from #post and leave its registration intact: construction still proves a read-back is registered for the effect-reservation companion, and assertObservedWriteSetIsDerived still finds the written relation derived, so before this packet the posting committed with the reservation never observed. entries.name: verifier-returns-without-observing
entries.claim: A VERIFIER THAT RETURNS WITHOUT OBSERVING ITS RELATION. The call is present and the registration is intact; the posted-stock balance verifier simply returns before reading a row, which is what a call-site-only mechanism would count as executed. A token is minted from a row PostgreSQL returned, never from the function having been entered, so no token exists for the balance relation the trigger wrote and the posting refuses naming it. Distinct from the deleted-call entry by relation: this red names the balance table, that one names the reservation table.

entries.name: token-minted-for-an-unwritten-relation
entries.claim: THE SECOND DIRECTION. A token is a claim about this transaction's writes, and the comparison is an EQUALITY, so a verifier claiming a relation the posting did not write is refused rather than read as extra coverage. The movement read-back is registered for the partitioned PARENT as well as its partitions, and PostgreSQL counts a routed insert on the leaf only (measured), so minting the parent from the registration -- a relation the verifier is registered for but no row came back from -- is a token for an unwritten relation. Without this direction a verifier could cover a relation by naming it.

entries.name: token-minted-by-an-unregistered-verifier
entries.claim: COVERAGE MAY ONLY BE CLAIMED BY THE READ-BACK CONSTRUCTION PROVED FOR THE RELATION. The reservation rows are minted under the movement read-back's name, so the reservation relation carries a token from a verifier the registry does not bind to it. The ledger is checked against the same registry construction proved complete, and a token from the wrong verifier refuses; otherwise any verifier that happened to read a relation could stand in for the one that compares its columns.

entries.name: active-release-fact-checked-after-the-receipt-lookup
entries.claim: ROUND-1 REVIEW FINDING, and the reason the first candidate was BLOCKed. This restores the reviewed candidate's PLACEMENT exactly: the capability-fact check is moved back to after the stored-receipt lookup and its replay return. Nothing is deleted -- a fresh posting is still checked, so the declared-version-one control stays GREEN -- and the one property that varies is WHEN the check runs. `findReceipt` keys on tenant, environment, capability and idempotency key only, never on the release a receipt was recorded under, so with the check placed later an operator on a release declaring version 1 replays a key recorded under version 2 and is served that version-2 result with no mismatch announced. This entry and `active-release-fact-never-read` are the discriminating pair the review asked for: that one proves the check exists, this one proves it runs before anything can return.

entries.name: recorded-at-floor-absent
entries.claim: `5g3-prog` A3, THE SUBJECT ABSENT. `recordedAt` is a wall-clock sample and this machine steps its clock backward under load; the comparator orders by `effectiveAt` first, so a backward step is invisible to the negative-stock check. Remove the floor and the specimen posting -- recorded earlier than the movement already on its stock identity, effective later -- is ADMITTED, exactly as before this packet: by effective time the prefix is (+10, -5) and never negative. What the admission then publishes is an as-of read, at a recorded-time horizon between the two, showing -5 under a policy that refuses negative stock. Silent until someone reads history, which is why it is Band A rather than visible-on-use.

entries.name: comparator-drops-the-movement-id-tie-break
entries.claim: `5g3-prog` A2, and the finding was that this kill existed only as PROSE: ADR-0027's table and the test's own assertion message named the mutation, and no manifest entry ran it. The global movement order is a seven-field tuple whose LAST discriminator is `movementId`; without it two movements identical in all six other fields compare EQUAL, `toSorted` is stable, and the order becomes an artifact of input sequence rather than a total order. That is what makes a posting's admission decision reproducible, so an unstable tie-break is a silent divergence between two runs over the same facts.

kills.expected: removing the production comparator movementId branch must reverse this verdict

entries.name: negative-stock-stops-sorting-persisted-with-planned
entries.claim: `5g3-prog` A2, second entry, and a DIFFERENT property from the comparator one: that the negative-stock check orders the persisted movements TOGETHER WITH the planned ones under that comparator, rather than checking the planned ones after the persisted ones. Remove the combined sort and the two sets stay in concatenation order -- every persisted row first -- so a planned debit that must sort BEFORE a persisted credit at the same instant is evaluated after it, the running prefix never goes negative, and a posting that has to be refused COMMITS. The specimen is built to discriminate exactly this: `sourceId` `a-planned-debit` sorts before `z-persisted-credit` at an identical effectiveAt and recordedAt.
